reply_text:
Done. I can now read `*claude-repl:claude-4*` with emacsclient, read-only, and I've saved the method to memory.

Line 1265 changes how I read your instruction. It says: "split `runtime.lisp` up directly and set up the working environment for agents the way you like it". It was part of the **Lisp** push in mfuton-sbcl, where codex-18 was put at claude-4's disposal. claude-4 acted on it straight away, splitting `runtime.lisp` in its own worktree (`/tmp/msb-runtime-split`).

My bell to claude-4 a few minutes ago applied your instruction to the **Python** parse-path seats. That's where tonight's dispatches have each seat create its own worktree and cold cache, and where the four wrong-reason test failures came from. The end of the buffer shows claude-4 already responding to it by drafting a `preamble6.md`.

If you meant "set up the environments yourself" to cover the Python seats too, my bell stands. If it was only about the Lisp work, I should tell claude-4 my bell overstated what you said. Which is it?
